To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the creation of a joint tertiary reserve energy market in Germany, Switzerland and Austria would lead to a reduction of system costs of around 10% in comparison with the current national markets.
the creation of a common reserve market between Germany, Austria and Switzerland can lead to significant cost savings.
a joint tertiary reserve energy market in the “Germalpinalpina” area is preferable over bilateral cooperation and leads to significant cost savings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question if a common reserve market between Germany, Austria, and Switzerland can be beneficial to the participating countries.
the question of whether a common market for tertiary reserve energy in the Germalpina zone would be beneficial for all participating countries.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the creation of one common tertiary reserve market is preferable to the bilateral coalitions, but that the benefits of a one market solution are rather small.
a common tertiary reserve market is a promising option to reduce overall system costs in the area of Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
the benefits of regional cooperation are not negligible and should be further explored in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a joint market for tertiary reserve energy is beneficial for the three countries involved.
the costs for tertiary reserve in Germany could be significantly reduced through cooperation.
the Germalpina zone is a promising approach to reduce the overall costs for tertiary reserve energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the costs of tertiary reserve energy can be reduced significantly by a common tertiary reserve market.
a joint tertiary reserve energy market between Germany, Austria and Switzerland can provide benefits for all three countries in terms of cost reduction.
there is a significant potential in the area of tertiary reserve energy for cooperation between Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
